title: Tokyo's Haneda Named World's Third Busiest Airport
paragraphs: Tokyo's Haneda Airport is now the third busiest airport in the world, according to a new ranking.
The ranking was made by Airports Council International, or ACI, a group that represents airports. It looked at the number of passengers at airports around the world in 2025.
In 2025, Haneda Airport had 91.7 million passengers. This was 6.7% more than in 2024. Haneda moved up from fourth place in 2024 to third place.

Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, in the US, was still the busiest airport in the world. It had 106.3 million passengers, although this was 1.6% fewer than the year before. Dubai International Airport was second, with 95.2 million passengers.

Dallas Fort Worth International Airport, in the US, moved down from third to fourth. Shanghai Pudong International Airport, in China, was fifth. It had 85 million passengers, and its number of passengers grew 10.7%, faster than any other airport in the top 10. The rest of the top 10 were Chicago O'Hare, London Heathrow, Istanbul, Guangzhou Baiyun and Denver.
Around the world, airports had about 9.8 billion passengers in 2025. This was 3.6% more than in 2024 and 7.3% more than in 2019, before the COVID-19 pandemic.

Justin Erbacci, the head of ACI World, said that there was growth in all regions, and that it was "fueled by international traffic." The ranking is based on data from more than 2,800 airports in over 180 countries.

It is important to remember that this ranking counts both international and domestic passengers. Haneda has many domestic flights inside Japan. When only international passengers are counted, a different ranking is used, and in 2026, Seoul's Incheon Airport was first in that ranking.
